evidence: backend.py:159-162: `if keep <= 0:` ... `return body[:max_chars]` (bare hard cut, no marker appended)
`_WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX: str = " … [truncated by reconciler]"` (rich_text.py:69) — 27 chars, so any configured ceiling of 1..26 reaches this branch
`comment_max_chars` coercer accepts the range 0..2147483647 (_config_schema.py:629), making sub-marker ceilings valid config, not impossible input
test_lowered_ceiling_is_honored uses ceiling 500 (test file:96) — well above the marker length, so it exercises only the normal `body[:keep] + suffix` path; no test uses a ceiling in 1..26
advisory.finding: The new `_truncate_dc_comment_body` `keep <= 0` branch — a bare hard cut with NO truncation marker when the configured ceiling is smaller than `_WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` (27 chars) — is untested. This branch is reachable via config (`comment_max_chars` coercer accepts 1..26), and a regression in its slice bound or marker handling would not be caught by any test.
scenarios: An administrator (or test config) sets comment_max_chars to a tiny value < len(marker); sanitize_comment/fit_comment must still respect the ceiling and produce byte-identical output on both send and differ sides for convergence.
